problem_motivation.content: The paper seeks to explain the anomalous bulk–monolayer Curie temperature behavior in VI3.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: aiming to identify the microscopic origin of the bulk–monolayer anomaly

problem_motivation.content: Weak interlayer interaction relative to intralayer interaction makes spin-wave theory challenging.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Note that the regime with interlayer interaction much weaker than the intralayer one represents a significant challenge for the spin-wave theory [12].

problem_motivation.content: The VI3 anomaly requires deeper theoretical study of finite-temperature magnetism and interlayer coupling.
problem_motivation.evidence_span:
This calls for a deeper theoretical investigation of finite-temperature magnetism in VI3 and the role
of interlayer coupling.

problem_motivation.content: Finite-temperature simulations comparing LO and HO separately and in mixture are missing.
problem_motivation.evidence_span:
Although basic properties of LO and HO atom types have been proposed,
a simulation comparing the finite-temperature behavior of these two types separately as well as in a mixture is
missing.

problem_motivation.content: No published calculation of bulk-VI3 interlayer interaction for the HO state is available.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: We are unaware of any published calculation of the interlayer interaction for bulk VI3 in the HO state.

problem_motivation.content: Estimating the interlayer exchange is challenging because of its strong sensitivity to geometry and stacking.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: This makes a qualified estimate of its value rather challenging.

prior_approach.content: First-principles calculations predicted two V atom types with very different magnetic anisotropies.
prior_approach.evidence_span: These types have strikingly different magnetic anisotropies, predicted to differ by more than an order of magnitude.

prior_approach.content: A recent spin-wave-theory study on VI3 predicted bulk TC correctly but low monolayer TC.
prior_approach.evidence_span:
a recent
study based on spin-wave theory on VI3, which correctly predicts TC for the bulk but reduces it to ∼14 K for
1ML [11]

Other calculations instead found the LO configuration to be the ground state.
prior_approach.evidence_span:
however, other calculations found the low-orbital-moment e′ 2
g
configuration (hereafter LO) to be the ground
state [24].

prior_approach.content: A recent DFT+U study found competing insulating states close in energy and sensitive to lattice distortions.
prior_approach.evidence_span:
a recent DFT+U study of VI3
and VCl3 found competing a1g- and e′

g

showed that symmetry-breaking lattice distortions can strongly reorganize their relative stability and orbital char-
acter [28]

prior_approach.content: The same distortion-biasing procedure was used previously in the authors' VBr3 study.
prior_approach.evidence_span:
this is the same procedure used
in our earlier VBr3 study. [19].

prior_approach.content: Camerano and Profeta showed that large optical-phonon displacement can switch the system to a different electronic surface and stabilize a symmetry-broken insulating state.
prior_approach.evidence_span:
A related sensitivity of the electronic state to lattice distortions has recently been investigated by Camerano and
Profeta [28]. They showed that a sufficiently large displacement along an optical Γ-point phonon eigenvector can
drive the system onto a different electronic energy surface and stabilize a symmetry-broken a1g-occupied insulating
state.

prior_approach.content: Torelli and Olsen previously analyzed 2D anisotropic Heisenberg ferromagnets with nearest-neighbor coupling and proposed an analytical TC formula.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Torelli and Olsen have studied magnetic order stability for a two-dimensional anisotropic Heisenberg ferromagnet with nearest neighbor interaction J1 only [43].

prior_approach.content: Mean-field theory predicts linear TC dependence on the total interaction sum J0.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The mean-field approach (MF) predicts the linear dependence of TC on the sum over all magnetic interactions with each site, J0 [46]:

prior_approach.content: Irkhin et al. developed a fluctuation-corrected self-consistent spin-wave expression for TC.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Studies of this problem within self-consistent spin-wave theory have led to a fluctuation-corrected self-consistent spin-wave-theory (FC-SWT) expression by Irkhin et al.[12].

prior_approach.content: Neutron spectroscopy and x-ray absorption/XMCD studies indicated coexistence of both V orbital configurations.
prior_approach.evidence_span: In this section we construct a minimal disorder model containing both V orbital configurations, whose coexistence has been indicated by neutron spectroscopy and x-ray absorption/x-ray magnetic circular dichroism measurements [26, 25].

prior_approach.content: Published ab initio values for anisotropy and intralayer exchanges were adopted from earlier studies.
prior_approach.evidence_span: For the SIA of V we adopt the published disparate values obtained by ab initio calculations, 15.9 meV for the HO type [22] and 0.4 meV (upper limit) for the LO type [41]. The three nearest-neighbor intralayer interactions for the LO case were taken from calculations by Gordon et al. [11].

prior_approach.content: Analogous stacking sensitivity of interlayer exchange has been demonstrated in other van der Waals trihalides.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Although direct experimental confirmation of this effect in VI3 is still lacking, analogous sensitivity has been demonstrated in other vdW trihalides [8, 9, 49, 10].

prior_approach.content: Earlier studies assumed 50% HO/LO concentration and reproduced observations sufficiently well.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Its authors have assumed, in both cases, a concentration of 50%, which has allowed the reproduction of observations with sufficient precision.

prior_limitation.content: Mean-field gives poor accuracy for small interlayer coupling and cannot capture Mermin-Wagner physics.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: The accuracy of this method is thus clearly worse for small JL. The mean-field approach obviously cannot handle the Mermin-Wagner behavior in the limit of vanishing both JL and magnetic anisotropy, where the correlation length diverges exponentially as T →0 [47].

prior_limitation.content: Mean-field only partially captures quasi-2D JL dependence because it treats exchanges only through an effective sum.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Even in the quasi-2D case of relatively small JL mean-field appears to capture the dependence only partially. The big difference between these two couplings is not correctly taken into account by mean-field theory, which utilizes only an effective sum of all exchange interactions with neighbors.

prior_limitation.content: The homogeneous defect-free FC-SWT model misses defect- and stacking-induced spatial exchange variations.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: This discrepancy is not unexpected since the fluctuation-corrected spin-wave expression assumes a homogeneous defect-free system and does not include defect- or stacking-induced spatial variations of exchange interactions.

rejected_alternative.evidence_span:
Presentation of few individual
values (as J′

of interlayer interaction is provided by their sum over all sites in one simulation cell layer, divided by the total number
of such sites N; we denote its value as the effective total interlayer interaction JL:

rejected_alternative.content: Although TC could be identified from heat capacity or Binder cumulant, the study instead uses the susceptibility peak as a practical criterion.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span:
Although the magnetic transition can also be identified from other quantities, such as heat capacity or Binder
cumulant, we use the peak position of the susceptibility as a practical criterion for TC.

rejected_alternative.content: The authors reject spatially segregated-domain modeling in favor of a random mixture because prior fitting models lacked segregation and showed disorder signatures.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: Note that Lane et al. [26] and Hovančík et al. [25] have used the term domains, which can evoke spatial segregation of the two types. However, the model used to fit the magnon spectra does not contain any segregation, and in fact signatures of disorder are encountered [26]. Therefore modeling the problem as a random mixture of two V types appears to be appropriate.

rejected_alternative.content: Explicit polaron simulations were not used because they are extremely computationally demanding.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: Simulations with polarons would probably be able to describe this situation quantitatively even more accurately, but these are extremely numerically demanding. Therefore, we leave it for the future as a potential step in improving our model.

inspiration_source.content: The mixed-bond approximation is inspired by Yang et al.'s orbital-dependent superexchange picture.
inspiration_source.evidence_span:
This approximation is motivated by the orbital-
dependent superexchange picture discussed by Yang et al.[22].

causal_claim.content: Increasing the fraction of high-anisotropy V sites increases the Curie temperature by suppressing transverse fluctuations.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The anisotropy contrast strongly affects thermal stability: increasing the fraction of high-anisotropy sites raises the energy cost of transverse spin fluctuations and increases TC.

causal_claim.content: An inhomogeneous V environment alters the interlayer super-superexchange network, weakening coherent interlayer magnetic order while keeping intralayer ferromagnetism robust.
causal_claim.evidence_span: At the same time, the interlayer super-superexchange network is modified by the inhomogeneous V environment. It becomes spatially non-uniform and can contain competing exchange pathways, weakening coherent interlayer magnetic order while preserving robust intralayer ferromagnetic correlations.

causal_claim.content: A near 1:1 ratio of the two V types reproduces the experimental bulk Curie temperature.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The experimental bulk value is reproduced when the ratio is close to 1:1

causal_claim.content: Sensitivity of TC to the HO/LO ratio implies that controlling relative occupations could tune the ordering temperature over a broad range.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The sensitivity of TC to the HO/LO ratio suggests that the ordering temperature of VI3 could be tuned over a broad range by controlling the relative occupation of the two vanadium configurations.

causal_claim.content: Twisting or changing stacking alters interlayer interaction paths and strongly affects interlayer magnetic interactions.
causal_claim.evidence_span: In these cases, the geometry of individual layers is not significantly changed, but the different geometry of interaction paths between atoms of different layers will strongly affect the magnetic interactions between layers [5].

causal_claim.content: Reducing CrI3 thickness changes the sign of interlayer exchange so bilayers become antiferromagnetically coupled.
causal_claim.evidence_span: For example, in CrI3 even sign of the interlayer magnetic exchange changes when the system is thin enough, so that in a bilayer individual layers are antiferromagnetically coupled [6].

causal_claim.content: Different stackings significantly change interlayer coupling.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Different stackings lead to significant changes in interlayer coupling [7].

causal_claim.content: Pressure mainly changes vdW gap size and thus interlayer coupling.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Pressure experiments are expected to affect mainly the vdW gap size and thus again the interlayer coupling.

causal_claim.content: If pressure induces stacking changes, its effect is enhanced because stacking can change the sign of interlayer interaction.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The pressure effect can be further enhanced if it leads to stacking change, different stacking has been seen to again change the sign of interlayer interaction in CrI3 [8, 9], CrBr3 [10]. or VI3 [11].

causal_claim.content: Removing interlayer coupling should destabilize order and lower TC.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Its absence should therefore destabilize the magnetic order and reduce the critical temperature (TC).

causal_claim.content: Different orbital occupations in HO and LO can lead to very different intralayer and interlayer exchange interactions.
causal_claim.evidence_span:
As HO and LO solutions
contain different orbital occupations, it may lead to strikingly different exchange interaction of both intralayer and
interlayer types.

causal_claim.content: High-momentum states have exceptionally large magnetic anisotropy.
causal_claim.evidence_span:
They also differ in magnetic anisotropy, which in fact reaches exceptionally high values for the
high momentum states [22, 23].

causal_claim.content: Local lattice perturbations from polarons can account for coexistence of high- and low-momentum states and resulting inhomogeneity.
causal_claim.evidence_span:
The existence of both high-
and low momentum states in real samples and the resulting inhomogeneity can, in fact, be ascribed to the local lattice
perturbations introduced by polarons.

causal_claim.content: Changing the ratio of the two V types causes a large change in TC.
causal_claim.evidence_span:
Our results show that variation of the
ratio between different V types can cause a rather large change in TC.

causal_claim.content: The dependence of the mixed-bond exchange on arithmetic averaging is justified because orbital-dependent hopping contributes twice for HO-HO, zero for LO-LO, and once for HO-LO.
causal_claim.evidence_span:
This approximation is motivated by the orbital-
dependent superexchange picture discussed by Yang et al.[22]. This picture rests on the relatively stronger hopping

1 occupied pair (HO-HO case), where it contributes twice, while it does not contribute for the e′
g
2 pair
(LO-LO) case. For the a1g1e′
g
2 occupied pair (HO-LO) it contributes once, e.g. by half the difference between
HO-HO and LO-LO.

causal_claim.content: Higher single-ion anisotropy raises Curie temperature, with a sub-linear trend that saturates at large anisotropy.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Figure 2 shows that the critical temperature increases monotonically with K, but the dependence is sub-linear and would tend to saturate at larger anisotropy (above the examined range).

causal_claim.content: At very low anisotropy, magnetic order is mainly stabilized by interlayer interaction.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Note that for the minimum anisotropy (approaching the Heisenberg limit), the magnetic order is stabilized mainly by the interlayer interaction addressed in the next section.

causal_claim.content: Difference in anisotropy between the two V configurations can nearly double TC.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The two possible configurations of V correspond to the lower and upper boundary of the SIA range shown in Fig. 2 , and the difference between them can therefore lead to a change of TC by almost a factor of 2.

causal_claim.content: Increasing interlayer coupling shifts magnetization curves and transition temperature upward.
causal_claim.evidence_span: As shown in Fig. 3(a), the magnetization curves shift systematically to higher temperature as JL increases. The corresponding transition temperature rises nearly monotonically over the full range of couplings considered, as summarized in Fig. 3(b).

causal_claim.content: Sensitivity of TC to interlayer coupling is consistent with the observed pressure dependence of TC in VI3.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This sensitivity due to interlayer coupling is also consistent with the experimentally observed pressure dependence of TC in VI3 [45].

causal_claim.content: Interlayer exchange depends strongly on electronic configuration, even changing sign between HO and LO cases.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The values obtained (Tab. 1) highlight its sensitivity also to the electronic configuration, as the sign also differs for the two cases considered.

causal_claim.content: Because JL can change sign with small distortions, polarons can cause strong cancellation of interlayer exchange on average.
causal_claim.evidence_span: However, the fact that it may change sign upon small distortion means that in the presence of polarons there will be a large cancelation on average, and this key feature is also captured by our model with two V types.

causal_claim.content: Increasing HO concentration raises the bulk ordering temperature from about 24 K to about 70 K.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Increasing CHO systematically increases the bulk ordering temperature, from approxi-mately 24 K in CHO = 20% to approximately 70 K in CHO = 80% .

causal_claim.content: Changing HO concentration alters the number and connectivity of HO-HO, LO-LO, and HO-LO interlayer exchange paths.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Changing CHO also changes the number and connectivity of the exchange paths between layers HO–HO, LO–LO, and HO–LO.

causal_claim.content: Different strengths and signs of interlayer paths make the interlayer exchange field spatially nonuniform.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Since these paths can carry different exchange strengths and, in some cases, different signs, the interlayer exchange field becomes spatially non-uniform.

causal_claim.content: Lower HO fraction in the anisotropy-only control shifts the magnetization drop to lower temperature.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Figure 5 shows the temperature-dependent normalized magnetization for the anisotropy-only control model (HO+MLH). As CHO decreases, the magnetization drop shifts to a lower temperature.

causal_claim.content: Anisotropy contrast alone is sufficient to reduce TC even when exchange remains homogeneous.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Thus, even when the exchange network is kept homogeneous, replacing HO sites with MLH sites is sufficient to reduce the Curie temperature, as seen in Fig. 5(b).

causal_claim.content: Including environment-dependent exchange further lowers TC, especially in LO-rich compositions.
causal_claim.evidence_span: When the exchange parameters are also allowed to depend on the atomic type, the original HO+LO model, the Curie temperature decreases more strongly, particularly in the LO-rich region (shown in both 4(b) and Fig. 5(b)).

causal_claim.content: At high HO concentration, both models converge because HO sites dominate magnetic order and LO sites cannot sustain extended fluctuations on their own.
causal_claim.evidence_span: On the other hand, at high CHO the two models approach nearly the same transition temperature. This indicates that the magnetic order of the system becomes dominated by HO sites in this regime, and LO sites cannot achieve extended fluctuations on their own sublattice.

causal_claim.content: Changing concentration reorganizes the topology of the interlayer exchange network rather than merely replacing site types.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Figure 6 shows that changing the concentration does not simply replace one type of V site with another; it reorganizes the topology of the interlayer exchange network.

causal_claim.content: As LO fraction increases, low-orbital and mixed interlayer paths become more frequent and introduce competing magnetic channels.
causal_claim.evidence_span: As the fraction of low-orbital sites increases, low-orbital and mixed interlayer paths become more frequent. Because these V–I· · · I–V geometries involve different orbital characters, they can contribute differently to the effective interlayer exchange and introduce competing magnetic channels.

causal_claim.content: Changing occupation of V types is expected to strongly alter TC because of anisotropy variation.
causal_claim.evidence_span: In particular, the variation with anisotropy allows us to expect a large change in TC when the occupation of different types of V changes.

causal_claim.content: Frustrated, nonuniform interlayer exchange weakens global magnetic coherence and suppresses bulk ordering temperature.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This frustration weakens the global magnetic coherence of the bulk crystal and suppresses the ordering temperature.

causal_claim.content: In the mixed system, interlayer interaction does not significantly raise TC over the monolayer because competing interlayer pathways are absent in monolayers.
causal_claim.evidence_span: For this mixture, the presence of interlayer interaction does not significantly increase the critical temperature compared to the monolayer case, where competing interlayer pathways are absent.

causal_claim.content: Variation in the ratio of V types can cause a large change in TC.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Our results show that variation of the ratio between different V types can cause a rather large change in TC.

mechanism_principle.content: Higher-anisotropy sites raise the energy cost of transverse spin fluctuations, which explains the increase in TC.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: increasing the fraction of high-anisotropy sites raises the energy cost of transverse spin fluctuations and increases TC

mechanism_principle.content: Spatially non-uniform and competing interlayer exchange pathways are the reason coherent interlayer order is weakened.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: It becomes spatially non-uniform and can contain competing exchange pathways, weakening coherent interlayer magnetic order while preserving robust intralayer ferromagnetic correlations.

mechanism_principle.content: Without interlayer coupling, monolayers need anisotropy for long-range order because of the Mermin-Wagner theorem.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Due to the Mermin-Wagner theorem such truly 2D systems feature long-range magnetic order at sufficiently low temperatures only if magnetic anisotropy is present [3, 4]

mechanism_principle.content: In other cases, enhanced magnetism in thinner systems is usually linked to electronic-structure changes affecting intralayer magnetism, such as band flattening satisfying the Stoner criterion.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
Still, it is
typically connected with an associated change of electronic structure connected to intralayer magnetic properties,
for example, the flattening of bands so that the Stoner criterion may become satisfied in a thin layer rather than
bulk.

mechanism_principle.content: Because interlayer influence on intralayer properties is limited in vdW materials, the usual thin-layer electronic-structure explanation is less applicable.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: However, in vdW materials, the influence of different layers on intralayer properties is limited.

mechanism_principle.content: Which orbital state is favored depends on competition among correlations, lattice distortions, spin-orbit interaction, and Kugel-Khomskii orbital ordering.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
The preference for either of these
solutions depends on a delicate competition between electron correlations, lattice distortions, spin-orbit interaction,
and the Kugel-Khomskii orbital ordering mechanism [27].

mechanism_principle.content: Using susceptibility peak is appropriate because it coincides with a rapid loss of magnetization at the transition.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
This criterion is appro-
priate because the susceptibility shows a pronounced maximum at the transition, coinciding with a rapid loss of
magnetization M.

mechanism_principle.content: Out-of-plane anisotropy stabilizes ferromagnetism by suppressing transverse fluctuations and opening a magnon gap.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: A stronger out-of-plane anisotropy suppresses transverse spin fluctuations, opens a magnon gap, and therefore stabilizes the ferromagnetic state against thermal disorder.

mechanism_principle.content: Single-ion anisotropy enhances TC by increasing the energy cost of spin deviations, especially in layered magnets sensitive to thermal fluctuations.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Single-ion anisotropy increases the energy cost of spin deviations and thus controls the thermal stability of the ordered phase (enhances TC). The effect is particularly important in layered magnets, where reduced dimensionality makes the ordered phase more sensitive to thermal fluctuations.

mechanism_principle.content: Offset between analytical 2D and simulated quasi-2D TC curves is attributed to omitted interlayer interaction in the pure 2D model.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The two graphs can be seen as vertically shifted with respect to each other; this can be ascribed to the interlayer interaction missing in the pure 2D model.

mechanism_principle.content: Even weak interlayer coupling in a quasi-2D ferromagnet promotes coherence between layers and suppresses critical fluctuations.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This is the expected behavior of a quasi-two-dimensional ferromagnet: although the interlayer interaction is weak on the meV scale, it suppresses critical fluctuations and promotes coherence between neighboring layers.

mechanism_principle.content: Interlayer exchange is small and highly geometry-sensitive because it is mediated by extended V-I...I-V super-superexchange channels across the van der Waals gap.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The interlayer exchange is mediated by extended V–I· · · I–V super-superexchange channels across the van der Waals gap [48] and is therefore relatively small and highly sensitive to changes in the interlayer geometry and stacking registry; different stackings can even reverse its sign [11].

mechanism_principle.content: The concentration dependence of TC reflects competition between strong intralayer ferromagnetism and frustrated interlayer coupling.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The resulting concentration dependence TC(CHO) here reflects the competition between robust intralayer ferromagnetic correlations and frustrated interlayer coupling.

mechanism_principle.content: Replacing HO with low-anisotropy MLH lowers the cost of transverse fluctuations and weakens out-of-plane order.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This behavior is expected because the fraction of MLH sites increases, and MLH sites have a single-ion anisotropy much smaller than that of HO sites. The reduced anisotropy lowers the energy cost of transverse spin fluctuations and weakens the stability of the out-of-plane ordered state.

mechanism_principle.content: Exchange inhomogeneity is an added mechanism that reduces thermal stability of bulk magnetism.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This indicates that exchange inhomogeneity provides an additional mechanism for reducing the thermal stability of the bulk magnetic state.

mechanism_principle.content: TC reduction with decreasing HO fraction is not just anisotropy averaging; spatially varying exchange further suppresses ordering.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: These results show that the reduction of TC with decreasing CHO is not controlled by anisotropy averaging alone. The smaller anisotropy of LO sites weakens the local stabilization of the ordered moments, whereas the environment-dependent exchange modifies the connectivity of the HO–HO, LO–LO, and HO–LO exchange paths. As a result, the effective magnetic coupling becomes spatially non-uniform, further suppressing the bulk ordering temperature compared to that of the anisotropy-only model.

mechanism_principle.content: Coexistence of two orbital environments makes interlayer exchange channels inequivalent in strength and sign, producing a nonuniform network.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: When two local orbital environments coexist, interlayer exchange channels are no longer equivalent: like-site and mixed-site paths can differ in both strength and sign. The bulk interlayer coupling therefore forms a spatially non-uniform exchange network rather than a single homogeneous field.

mechanism_principle.content: Spatial variation in interlayer exchange reduces coherence between layers while leaving strong intralayer ferromagnetism intact, suppressing bulk TC.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
This provides a microscopic route for suppressing the bulk ordering temperature. In the homogeneous model, the presence of JL always enhances TC. However, in the mixed-orbital network, the spatial variation of J′
ij reduces the coherence of the interlayer exchange field while preserving strong intralayer ferromagnetic correlations.

mechanism_principle.content: In the mixed system, different anisotropies and perturbed interlayer geometry create competing interlayer pathways and frustration.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This coexistence represents a highly complex problem, where the components respond differently to thermal fluctuations, mainly due to their different anisotropy. The geometry of V–I· · · I–V interlayer super-superexchange is also strongly perturbed and leads to competing interlayer exchange pathways. The interlayer exchange network becomes spatially non-uniform and frustrated.

mechanism_principle.content: Among the differing properties of the two V types, anisotropy is the key factor for finite-temperature magnetization.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Among the different properties of these two types, the variation of anisotropy plays a key role in finite-temperature magnetization.

hypothesis_statement.content: The bulk–monolayer anomaly can be understood from the combined effects of single-ion anisotropy and exchange interactions in a system containing two V types.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Here, we use atomistic spin-dynamics simulations to study critical temperatures in VI3 from the combined perspective of single-ion anisotropy and exchange interactions, aiming to identify the microscopic origin of the bulk–monolayer anomaly. We consider a system composed of two V types with properties predicted by first-principles calculations.

hypothesis_statement.content: The work proposes that established HO/LO coexistence explains finite-temperature magnetic ordering, including the anomalous bulk–monolayer TC difference, through anisotropy contrast and spatially non-uniform interlayer exchange.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span:
Thus, the new contribution of the present work is to connect the established HO/LO coexistence picture
to finite-temperature magnetic ordering by showing how anisotropy contrast and spatially non-uniform interlayer
exchange affect TC, including the anomalous bulk–monolayer difference in VI3.

hypothesis_statement.content: The study will explain the bulk/monolayer TC difference from combined single-ion anisotropy and exchange interactions.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span:
In this paper, we use atomistic spin-dynamics simulations to understand the behavior of critical temperatures
in this system from the combined perspective of single-ion anisotropy and exchange interactions, with a focus on
identifying the microscopic origin of the bulk/monolayer VI3 TC difference.

hypothesis_statement.content: Weak interlayer coupling alone cannot account for the reduced bulk ordering temperature of VI3.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: The comparison suggests that weak interlayer coupling alone is not sufficient to explain the reduced bulk ordering temperature of VI3.

hypothesis_statement.content: A plausible polaron concentration could produce a similar balance of affected and unaffected V atoms in real VI3.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: To achieve a similar amount of both affected and unaf-fected V atoms, roughly 1 electron per 20 formula unit (f.u) is needed, which corresponds to the doping of 0.0125 electron per atom. Such doping appears to be plausible in real VI3 samples.

hypothesis_statement.content: A control model is introduced to isolate anisotropy contrast from exchange inhomogeneity.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: To separate the effect of anisotropy contrast from that of exchange inhomogeneity, we construct another model where we use a fictitious V configuration MLH (mixed LO and HO).

hypothesis_statement.content: Exfoliation may change excess charge, polaron concentration, and therefore HO concentration in monolayer VI3.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: The exfoliation used to obtain an ML VI3 [17] can lead to a change of the possible excess charge on the V atoms. Therefore, also the concentration of polarons and the concentration CHO may differ from the bulk value.

hypothesis_statement.content: Combined changes in anisotropy and exchange between the two V configurations can explain both bulk and monolayer VI3 behavior.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Thus, the combined change of single-ion anisotropy and exchange interactions between the two possible V configurations allows us to propose parameters that describe both bulk and ML VI3 behavior (shown in Fig. 7).

hypothesis_statement.content: Weak interlayer interactions in vdW magnets need not stabilize order; if spatially nonuniform or competing, they can instead suppress it.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Our findings emphasize that weak interlayer interactions in van der Waals magnets should not always be viewed as simple stabilizing perturbations; when they are spatially non-uniform or competing, they can instead suppress magnetic order.

hypothesis_statement.content: Bulk and monolayer TC differences can be explained by different concentrations of V atom types with different electronic configurations.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We have found that the different critical temperatures of the bulk and ML samples could be explained by a variation of the concentration of V atom types with different electronic configurations.

hypothesis_statement.content: Controlling HO/LO occupation should enable wide tuning of TC, by at least a factor of two.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Our results further suggest that controlling the relative occupation of the HO and LO V configurations could tune the Curie temperature TC over a wide range, with at least a factor of two differences between its upper and lower limits.

evidence_result.content: Changing the ratio of the two V types produces a substantial shift in Curie temperature.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Our results show that changing the ratio of the two V types can cause a substantial shift in TC.

evidence_result.content: A near 1:1 ratio reproduces the experimental bulk Curie temperature and agrees with experimental signs of coexisting V configurations.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The experimental bulk value is reproduced when the ratio is close to 1:1, consistent with two experimental indications of coexisting V configurations.

evidence_result.content: Finite-temperature magnetization behavior supports coexistence of two V configurations in VI3.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Thus, the finite-temperature magnetization behavior provides further support for the coexistence of two V configurations in VI3.

evidence_result.content: The experimentally observed monolayer Curie temperature is matched by a slightly modified V-type ratio.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The experimentally observed monolayer TC is obtained for a slightly modified ratio, which may be related to the polaron concentration.

evidence_result.content: Experiments observed HO-type vanadium, but reproducing x-ray spectra required including LO-type contributions.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
HO-type vanadium has been observed experimentally in VI3 samples, while inclusion of an LO-type con-
tribution was required to reproduce the measured x-ray absorption and x-ray magnetic circular dichroism spectra
[25].

evidence_result.content: Neutron scattering also indicated coexistence of HO and LO states.

30] and is also susceptible to stacking faults [31].

evidence_result.evidence_span: The analytical formula apparently captures the change of TC with reasonable precision, the largest difference to our simulation of quasi-2D system occurring for a low anisotropy.

evidence_result.content: For weak interlayer coupling the bulk approaches monolayer behavior, while strong coupling shifts the transition to about 70 K.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For the weakest interlayer coupling, JL = 0.14 meV, the bulk response approaches the monolayer limit. For the strongest coupling, JL = 0.95 meV, the transition is shifted to approximately 70 K.

evidence_result.content: FC-SWT gives TC values closer to experiment than mean field, but still too high.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The obtained values are closer to the experimental bulk value of about 50 K [18] than the mean-field result, but remain higher.

evidence_result.content: Second- and third-neighbor intralayer exchanges in VI3 are small and not significant here.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Notably, the 2nd and 3rd nearest-neighbor interactions appear to be small in VI3 and do not play a significant role compared to other effects considered here.

evidence_result.content: In mixed configurations, magnetization drops rapidly at the transition and susceptibility peaks clearly at the ordering temperature.
evidence_result.evidence_span: In Fig. 4(a), the temperature-dependent normalized magnetization and susceptibility are shown for the representative mixed configuration with various concentrations CHO. The magnetization decreases rapidly in the transition region, whereas the susceptibility shows a clear peak at the ordering temperature.

evidence_result.content: Matching the bulk TC implies an HO concentration of about 0.46 in the model.

Comparing the bulk TC with the prediction allows us to determine Cbulk
HO
=0.46 within the assumptions of our model.

evidence_result.evidence_span: The relatively moderate slope of the HO+MLH curve indicates that anisotropy contrast alone significantly changes the transition temperature, but exchange-related effects are also important.

evidence_result.content: The bulk-monolayer TC difference shrinks as HO concentration decreases, and for CHO below 0.4 the monolayer TC exceeds bulk TC.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Note that the difference between bulk and ML TC (shown in Fig. 4(b)) decreases with decreasing CHO, and therefore the stabilization due to intralayer exchange is less relevant as the competition between LO and HO type interaction becomes more balanced. For CHO < 0.4 the ML TC is even becoming higher than that of bulk.

evidence_result.evidence_span: Note that a comparison of surface and bulk-sensitive spectroscopies has revealed that occupation of the a1g level is more pronounced on surfaces [24, 50], again indicating volatility of the HO/LO concentration and probably higher concentration of the VI3 HO state when not in bulk.

evidence_result.content: Homogeneous-system calculations show how much TC can be modified by anisotropy and interlayer exchange across realistic parameter ranges.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The results show to what extent the critical temperature can be modified by single-site anisotropy and interlayer exchange.

HO

evidence_result.content: Finite-temperature magnetization behavior provides further evidence for coexistence of two V configurations in VI3.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Thus, we have provided further evidence for the picture of two coexisting V configurations in VI3, this time on the basis of finite-temperature magnetization behavior.

constraint.content: To model quasi-2D VI3, interactions between non-neighboring layers are neglected because interlayer exchange is much weaker than intralayer exchange.
constraint.evidence_span:
Because the interlayer exchange is much weaker than the
intralayer exchange, interactions between non-neighboring layers are neglected.

constraint.content: The calculations assume translational invariance along the c axis so exchange interactions are equivalent for all layers.
constraint.evidence_span:
In a quasi-2D system, boundaries may be neglected and the exchange
interactions are equivalent for all layers due to the translational invariance along the c axis.

constraint.evidence_span:
Because these two occupations are nearly degenerate but coupled to slightly

contradiction.content: Monolayer VI3 was reported to have a higher Curie temperature than bulk, contrary to the usual expectation about interlayer coupling.
contradiction.evidence_span: VI3 also shows an unusual thickness dependence: the reported monolayer Curie temperature, TC, is higher than that of the bulk, contrary to the usual expectation that interlayer coupling reinforces magnetic order.

contradiction.content: VI3 monolayer has higher TC than bulk, contrary to the usual expectation that monolayer TC should be lower.
contradiction.evidence_span:
Interestingly, an exception to this observation has recently been found in VI3, where 1ML TC reaches 60 K [17]

contradiction.evidence_span:
This finding is in striking contrast to a recent study based on spin-wave theory on VI3, which correctly predicts TC for the bulk but reduces it to ∼14 K for
